title: Scavenging for Coins in River Sewage
hook: Poor Victorian kids waded through raw river sewage for pennies.

scenes.text: In Victorian London, impoverished children called 'mudlarks' survived by scavenging the muddy banks of the River Thames at low tide.

scenes.voicedText: In Victorian London, impoverished children called 'mudlarks' survived by scavenging the muddy banks of the River Thames at low tide.

scenes.text: Barefoot and dressed in ragged burlap, they waded knee-deep through freezing black mud filled with raw sewage and industrial runoff.
scenes.imagePrompt: Wet cobblestone river stairs covered in green slime leading into murky brown river water beside stone bridges. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Barefoot and dressed in ragged burlap, they waded knee-deep through freezing black mud filled with raw sewage and industrial runoff.

scenes.text: They hunted for anything saleable: dropped copper pennies, pieces of coal, rusted iron nails, old bones, and rope fibers.

scenes.voicedText: They hunted for anything saleable: dropped copper pennies, pieces of coal, rusted iron nails, old bones, and rope fibers.

scenes.text: Hidden danger lurked everywhere: jagged broken glass, drowned carcasses, and sudden incoming tides that trapped children against river walls.

scenes.text: A lucky mudlark made barely three pennies a day—just enough to buy a crust of stale bread and a night in a lodging house.
